profile.summary: ProGen3 is a family of generative protein language models released by Profluent. Given a direction marker and an optional partial sequence, a model writes amino acids one at a time, in either the N-to-C or the C-to-N direction, and it can also fill in a span in the middle of a given sequence. The same models score an existing sequence by log-likelihood and perplexity, which is how the repository evaluates them on ProteinGym assays. Six checkpoints are published, from 112M to about 3B parameters, under a non-commercial weights licence.

summary_quotes.text: This repository contains code to access the ProGen3 family of models as well as cli interface to run these models for scoring and generation.
The model weights are released under a **non-commercial** usage license.
For CLM in N-to-C (forward) direction: residues from N direction (e.g. `1AAS`)
`log_likelihood` : The log likelihood of the sequence.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: ProGen3 is a sparse mixture-of-experts transformer. The 3B configuration has 24 layers, hidden size 1280, 16 attention heads, 8 experts with 2 chosen per token, SiLU-gated feed-forward blocks, RMS normalisation and rotary position embeddings. It is trained in both reading directions: a prompt starts with 1 for N-to-C or 2 for C-to-N, so the same model can extend a sequence from either end. A separate [GLM] prompt form asks the model to replace a named span of a given sequence with a chosen average number of residues, which is how infilling is done. Scoring averages the log-likelihood of the forward and reverse directions.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Six checkpoints are on the Hugging Face hub: progen3-112m, progen3-219m, progen3-339m, progen3-762m, progen3-1b and progen3-3b. Hugging Face counts their weights as 112,456,320, 219,677,184, 339,245,568, 762,885,888, 1,355,871,232 and 2,989,920,000 parameters, so the names round the true counts (the 1B checkpoint is about 1.36B and the 3B about 2.99B). None is gated. A result should name the checkpoint and its Hugging Face revision, and for generation also the temperature and top-p, since the README's example sets 0.85 and 0.95 rather than relying on defaults. This page read the 3B checkpoint at revision f2c6b565.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Generative protein language model, a sparse mixture-of-experts transformer trained in both sequence directions, used for generation, infilling and sequence scoring.
facts.source_locator: README: introduction, Prompt File Format; config.json

quotes.text: cli interface to run these models for scoring and generation

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Mixture-of-experts transformer. In the 3B configuration: 24 layers, hidden size 1280, intermediate size 3840, 16 attention heads, 8 experts with 2 per token and switch routing, SiLU gated MLP, RMS norm, rotary embeddings, vocabulary of 134 tokens.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: For scoring: a FASTA file of sequences, each with a unique id and at most 8190 residues. For generation: a CSV prompt file with an id, a sequence starting with the direction marker 1 or 2, and minimum and maximum new token counts. Infilling prompts add a [GLM] span specification.
facts.source_locator: README: Input File Formats, Prompt File Format; examples/generations/prompts.csv

quotes.text: where each sequence has a unique id and maximum length of 8190 residues

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Scoring writes a CSV with sequence_id, log_likelihood and perplexity. Generation writes two FASTA files per prompt: {id}.gen.fasta with the raw generated tokens and {id}.seq.fasta with the valid full N-to-C sequences.
facts.source_locator: README: Input File Formats, Generation CLI

quotes.text: First is `{id}.gen.fasta` which contains the raw tokens generated by the model for each generated sequence (not containing the prompt).
the `seq.fasta` files only contain a subset of `gen.fasta` file generations since some of the generations in `gen.fasta` file may be invalid

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: 112,456,320 (progen3-112m), 219,677,184 (219m), 339,245,568 (339m), 762,885,888 (762m), 1,355,871,232 (1b) and 2,989,920,000 (3b), counted by Hugging Face from the published safetensors files. These are total parameters of a sparse model, not the parameters used per token.

run_guide.summary: Install the repository on a GPU machine and score one protein sequence with the 3B checkpoint.
prerequisites: At least one GPU. The developers tested only A100 or H100 cards with at least 40GB of VRAM, and say earlier GPUs may not work because bf16 and flash attention kernels are needed.
The install script builds megablocks 0.7.0 and flash-attn 2.7.4.post1 from source, so a CUDA toolchain is needed. A prepared Docker image is offered instead.
The weights are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: non-commercial use only. They are not gated.

steps.title: Score one sequence
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch

from progen3.modeling import ProGen3ForCausalLM
from progen3.batch_preparer import ProGen3BatchPreparer
from progen3.scorer import ProGen3Scorer

model = ProGen3ForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Profluent-Bio/progen3-3b", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16)
model = model.eval().to("cuda:0")
batch_preparer = ProGen3BatchPreparer()

sequence = "MALWMRLLPLLALLALWGPDPAAAFVNQHLCGSHLVEALYLVCGERGFFYTPKTRREAEDLQVGQVELGGGPGAGSLQPLALEGSLQKRGIVEQCCTSICSLYQLENYCN"

scorer = ProGen3Scorer(model=model)
scores = scorer.score_batch(sequences=[sequence])
print(scores["log_likelihood"][0])
PY
steps.explanation: The README's interactive example, wrapped in a shell heredoc and reduced to the scorer part. It downloads the 3B weights from Hugging Face on first use. The README's logits example is left out.

limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
A GPU with at least 40GB of VRAM is assumed; the sources give no figure for the smaller checkpoints.
The weights licence forbids commercial use.
Building megablocks and flash-attn from source can be slow and needs a matching CUDA toolchain; the Docker image is the alternative the README offers.

notes: The bioRxiv preprint (10.1101/2025.04.15.649055) returned HTTP 429 on two attempts and was not read, so coverage is limited. The record's own description says up to 46 billion parameters and 1.5 trillion training tokens; nothing in the sources read supports either figure, and the largest released checkpoint is about 2.99B parameters. The weights licence (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) differs from the code licence (Apache-2.0), so a commercial user cannot use these weights. The structured context_length 8190 is the scoring limit from the README, not the configuration's max_position_embeddings of 65536.
